newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer ahead of LME stock report.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer ahead of LME stock report.

text.p: COMEX copper brushed aside its opening weakness to end firmer as the market awaited Tuesday's LME stock report, with expectations of a slight drawdown, traders said.
"I think we may have gone through the nearby correction," said Fred Demler of E D and F Man International.

But there was unease in the market about the LME December option declaration next week. "There is a lot of concern about not well placed shorts in the early part of December being squeezed," Demler said.

The London Clearing House doubled the cash/three months spread margin on LME copper futures to $3,750 per lot, seen by some as a move to cool speculative activity in a market where exchange inventories have shrunk to six year lows.
But during Monday's session the LME backwardation widened by about $15 to $173 to $183.
March COMEX, now with most-open interest, settled 1.15 cents firmer at 101.95 cents per pound, traded 102.00 to 99.30 cents. December went out 1.35 cents firmer at 105.90 cents.
The CFTC's Commitment of Traders report released late Friday indicated that in COMEX copper futures, the speculators were still heavily long, and commercials short.
In week ended November 19, speculators held 14,019 long positions and 4,103 short positions. The commercials held 43,066 short positions and 21,721 long positions.
The long to short ratios were little changed from the previous week.
COMEX trading volume on Monday was estimated at 15,000 lots, up from Friday's official 10,793 lots.
COMEX stocks Monday rose 664 short tons to 40,351 tons.
COMEX is closed on Thursday and Friday because of the Thanksgiving holiday.
